'''Mulligatawny''' ({{IPAc-en|audio=GT Mulligatawny.ogg|ˌ|m|ʌ|l|ɪ|g|ə|ˈ|t|ɔː|n|i}}) is a [[soup]] which originated from {{lang|ta-Latn|[[rasam (dish)|rasam]]}}<ref>{{cite book |last=Iyer |first=Raghavan |author-link=Raghavan Iyer (chef) |title=On the Curry Trail: Chasing the Flavor That Seduced the World |publisher=[[Workman Publishing Company|Workman Publishing]] |location=New York |year=2022 |isbn=978-1523511211 |oclc=1374192575 |p=138}}</ref> in [[Tamil cuisine]], though much transformed during its adoption into [[Anglo-Indian cuisine]]. The name originates from the [[Tamil language|Tamil]] words {{lang|ta-Latn|miḷagu}} ({{wikt-lang|ta|மிளகு}} 'black pepper'), and {{lang|ta-Latn|thanneer}} ({{wikt-lang|ta|தண்ணீர்}}, 'water'); literally, "pepper-water".<ref name=":0">{{Cite book |last=Clarkson |first=Janet |title=Soup : a global history |date=2010 |publisher=Reaktion |isbn=978-1-86189-774-9 |location=London |pages=118 |oclc=642290114 }}</ref> 

Main ingredients commonly include [[Chicken as food|chicken]], [[mutton]], and [[lentil]]s.<ref name=":1" />
